---
format:
  revealjs:
    theme:
      - default
      - assets/theme.scss
    width: 1600
    height: 900
    center: false
    slide-number: c/t
    hash: true
    menu: true
    progress: true
    controls: true
    transition: fade
    embed-resources: false
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
params:
  config_file: "presentation.yml"
  project_root: "."
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/presentation_helpers.R")
cfg <- read_presentation_config(params$config_file, params$project_root)
summary_object <- load_presentation_summary(cfg)
spict <- if (identical(cfg$data$adapter, "spict")) {
  extract_spict_context(summary_object)
} else {
  NULL
}
```

## {.title-slide}

::: {.title-kicker}
`r cfg$project$meeting`
:::

::: {.title-heading}
`r cfg$project$title`
:::

::: {.title-subtitle}
`r cfg$project$subtitle`
:::

::: {.title-footer}
::: {.title-logo-wrap}
<img src="assets/HI_logo_farger_engelsk.png" class="title-logo" alt="Institute of Marine Research logo" />
:::

::: {.title-meta}
`r paste(cfg$project$authors, collapse = ", ")`  
`r cfg$project$organisation`  
`r cfg$project$date`
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Open with the purpose of the presentation in one sentence. State whether the
audience is being asked to decide, discuss, or simply understand something.
:::

## Start with the story

::: {.takeaway}
`r cfg$project$story`
:::

:::: {.process-flow}
::: {.flow-step}
::: {.card-title}
1\. Question
:::

What does the audience need to understand or decide?
:::

::: {.flow-step}
::: {.card-title}
2\. Evidence
:::

Which chart, table, or diagram makes the answer credible?
:::

::: {.flow-step}
::: {.card-title}
3\. Implication
:::

What should the audience remember when the slide is gone?
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Replace this starter slide after agreeing on the narrative spine. A strong deck
reveals the structure early, especially when the later slides contain technical
detail.
:::

## Results update when the source project reruns

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Analysis project
:::

Model fitting, diagnostics, and annual updates remain in the scientific project.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Compact result object
:::

The presentation reads one stable summary file generated by the analysis workflow.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Quarto source
:::

Claims, notes, charts, and tables stay readable and editable in `presentation.qmd`.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Rendered artifacts
:::

Rerender HTML for presenting and PDF for review or archiving.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
For SPiCT projects, the input is the annual `sum_<stock>_spict_<year>.rds`
summary object written by the assessment workflow.
:::

## Trajectories should carry the argument

```{r}
#| label: fig-spict-trajectories
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.6
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```

::: {.small-note}
Figure caption
:::

::: {.notes}
Charts should be generated from the compact result object. Use the analysis
project for complex plotting functions and call those functions here when
possible.
:::

## Compare scenarios in one table

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scenarios
knitr::kable(
  scenario_table(spict),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

::: {.takeaway}
State the decision-facing comparison in one sentence.
:::

::: {.notes}
Keep tables narrow enough to read from the back of the room. Put the full
scenario table in an appendix if more columns are needed.
:::

## End with what should stick

:::: {.takeaway-grid}
::: {.takeaway-card}
::: {.card-title}
Finding
:::

State the most important empirical result.
:::

::: {.takeaway-card}
::: {.card-title}
Interpretation
:::

Explain why that result matters.
:::

::: {.takeaway-card}
::: {.card-title}
Next action
:::

Ask for the discussion, decision, or follow-up you need.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Do not end on a generic thank-you slide. End on the message the audience should
remember.
:::
